en: The Banaue Rice Terraces act as a giant inclined plane, making it easier for farmers to carry heavy harvests up the mountain.
Jeepney brake pads use high friction to stop the heavy vehicle safely when the driver presses the brake pedal.
Galileo Galilei proved that gravity accelerates all falling objects equally by dropping different weights from the Leaning Tower of Pisa.
Ancient Chinese sailors used a magnetic compass with a lodestone needle to navigate the oceans by aligning with Earth's magnetic poles.
Alessandro Volta created the first true battery, called the voltaic pile, by stacking alternating zinc and copper discs separated by saltwater.
Sir Isaac Newton demonstrated that white sunlight contains all colors of the rainbow by passing it through a glass prism.
Musicians play the traditional Filipino kulintang by striking its brass gongs, which produce sound waves through rapid physical vibrations.
Mayon Volcano transfers intense thermal energy to the surrounding environment through conduction when its hot lava touches cooler rocks.
The Bangui Wind Turbines in Ilocos Norte convert the kinetic energy of moving ocean winds into useful electrical energy.
A standard wooden nutcracker acts as a second-class lever, multiplying your hand's force to crack hard walnut shells.
The water stored behind the San Roque Dam possesses high gravitational potential energy before it flows down to spin turbines.
William Sturgeon invented the first electromagnet by wrapping a bare copper wire around a varnished iron core to create a temporary magnet.
